method.title: How the calculator works
method.p1: Daily protein in grams is your body weight in kilograms multiplied by grams of protein per kilogram. The calculator shows a range for each goal:
method.r0: Adult baseline: 0.83 g/kg a day, the EFSA reference intake for adults.
method.r1: Weight loss: 1.2–1.6 g/kg a day, the range the 2026 International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) position stand gives for the general population.
method.r2: Strength training: 1.6–2.2 g/kg a day, the 2026 ISSN weight-reduction stand's range when dieting with resistance training.
method.p2: Body weight is capped at 100 kg, as in Calcalou, so results stay practical at higher weights. These ranges are general guidance for healthy adults, not medical advice; pregnancy and breastfeeding need individual advice.
method.source: Sources: EFSA, Dietary Reference Values for protein, EFSA Journal 2012;10(2):2557, doi:10.2903/j.efsa.2012.2557. Aragon AA et al. International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: diets for body weight reduction. J Int Soc Sports Nutr 2026;23(1):2740266, doi:10.1080/15502783.2026.2740266.
app.title: Your protein goal in Calcalou
app.text: Calcalou 1.7 can set your protein goal from body weight and shows the calculation, for example 72 kg × 1.2 g/kg = 86 g. Adjust it from 0.8 to 2.0 g/kg or enter your own number, then log protein by hand, from a barcode or from an AI photo scan and watch it beside your calories.
faq.how.q: How is daily protein calculated from body weight?
faq.how.a: Multiply your weight in kilograms by grams of protein per kilogram. At 72 kg, 0.83 g/kg is 60 g, 1.2 g/kg is 86 g and 2.2 g/kg is 158 g.
faq.need.q: How much protein do I need per day?
faq.need.a: It depends on your body, goals and health. For adults the EFSA reference intake is 0.83 g/kg a day. The 2026 ISSN position stand gives 1.2–1.6 g/kg for weight loss and 1.6–2.2 g/kg when resistance training is included. This is general guidance, not medical advice.
faq.active.q: Do I need more protein to lose weight or build muscle?
faq.active.a: The 2026 International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand gives 1.2–1.6 g/kg a day for weight loss and 1.6–2.2 g/kg with resistance training. Which amount suits you depends on your situation, so ask a doctor or a registered dietitian.
faq.cap.q: Why does the calculator stop at 100 kg?
faq.cap.a: Calcalou counts at most 100 kg of body weight for a protein goal, so results stay practical at higher weights. Above 100 kg the calculator shows the result for 100 kg; ask a dietitian for a goal that fits you.
faq.accuracy.a: It gives ranges for a healthy adult from your weight alone. It does not know your height, body composition, activity or health. It is not medical advice: talk to a doctor or a registered dietitian before a big change to your diet.
